hero.h1: 24/7 Emergency Plumbing in Highland Park, IL
hero.sub: When water is coming into your home, you need a plumber who picks up and shows up. Our phone line is open 24/7, including nights, weekends and holidays, and our plumbers serve Highland Park and the North Shore.

img.alt: Homeowner on the phone while water leaks from the pipe under her kitchen sink into a bucket

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.intro: You need an emergency plumber when a problem has to be handled right now to limit damage or risk. Some emergencies are impossible to miss. Others are hiding behind walls or under older pipes.

tiles.body: Sewage coming up through a floor drain, tub or toilet. Stop using water and call. Don't think about it in flooding terms only, a worsening clog can be a system failure you're not seeing yet.
When a pipe lets go, every minute counts. Shut off the main water supply if you can and call immediately.

tiles.h3: Sump Pump or Ejector Pump Failure
tiles.body: Storm hit, the basement is flooding and the pump is dead. Call now, not tomorrow when the damage is done.
No hot water is inconvenient. Active leaking or strange noises from the tank is an emergency. The difference matters.
Don't troubleshoot this one. If you smell gas, get out and call your gas provider or 911 from outside. We'll handle the repair once it's safe.

tiles.h3: Hidden Leak or Water Line Issue
tiles.body: Wet walls, a higher water bill, soft spots in the floor. Not all leaks announce themselves. If something feels off, it probably is.

blocks.h2: The Emergencies We See in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: The median Highland Park home was built in 1963, and about 1 in 4 went up before 1940. Older plumbing, mature trees and long Lake County winters shape what goes wrong here.

items.h3: Frozen and Burst Pipes in Winter
items.body: Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and they can [split and flood a basement](/highland-park/burst-pipe-repair) once they thaw. Know where your main shutoff is before you need it.

items.h3: Backups From Roots and Old Clay
items.body: Roots from ravines and tree-lined streets get into older clay sewer lines. In Highland Park, the homeowner owns the private line from the house to the city main, so a [backup](/highland-park/sewage-line-backup-services) there is yours to fix.

Heavy rain and spring snowmelt can [push water into Highland Park basements](/highland-park/basement-flooding). A failed [sump pump](/highland-park/sump-pumps) during a storm is one of the most urgent calls we take.

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How fast can you get to my home in Highland Park?
items.preview: Call any time. We'll give you a realistic arrival window on the phone.
items.answer: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays. Our plumbers serve Highland Park and the North Shore around the clock. Arrival times depend on the day and call volume, but we'll give you a realistic window when you're on the phone and get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: What should I do while waiting for an emergency plumber?
items.preview: Stop the water at the nearest valve or the main. For gas, get out and call from outside.
items.answer: Stop the water first if you can. Shut off the supply valve closest to the problem, under the sink, behind the toilet or at the water heater. If you can't isolate it, shut off the main. If it's a gas leak, don't touch anything: get everyone out and call from outside. Once you're safe, call us and we'll walk you through the next steps.

items.q: How do I shut off my water in an emergency?
items.preview: Find the main shutoff near your water meter. Turn it clockwise to stop water to the whole house.
items.answer: Every home has a main shutoff valve, usually near the water meter in the basement or a utility room. Turning it clockwise stops water to the whole house. In an older Highland Park home, find and test it before you need it. Individual fixtures have their own shutoff valves under sinks, behind toilets and behind the washer.

items.q: What counts as a plumbing emergency?
items.preview: Sewage backups, burst pipes, active flooding, failed sump pumps, leaking water heaters and gas leaks.
items.answer: Any situation that needs to be handled right away to prevent damage, a health risk or loss of essential service. Sewage backing up, a burst or frozen pipe, active flooding, a failed sump pump during a storm, a leaking water heater or a suspected gas leak all qualify. If you're unsure, call. We'd rather you check than wait while damage spreads.

items.q: Do you offer financing for emergency repairs?
items.preview: Yes. Flexible payment plans are available through trusted financial partners.
items.answer: Yes. We offer flexible payment plans through trusted financial partners. If the cost of an emergency repair is more than you're prepared for right now, ask your technician about financing options when they're on-site. Subject to credit approval.
